- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if price is falling.
- After sharp price spikes, model frequently overshoots in the next few days; apply a downward correction of 5–10% for the immediate next period.
- Model shows persistent lag in mean reversion — if price is below 30-day moving average, forecast should be slightly above; if above, slightly below.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often misses the “late surge” phase (last 5–7 days) — increase forecast sensitivity to recent sentiment and price momentum.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive within 3–5 days, model tends to ignore the shift; adjust forecast upward by 2–5% if sentiment turns bullish.
- Avoid overreacting to single-day sentiment spikes — model often overcorrects; use 3–5 day sentiment average for smoothing.
